card: Bitcoin Core currently serves cached compact blocks for the latest tip using a single shared nonce across all peers. An adversary connected over multiple networks, such as clearnet and Tor, can compare nonces in compact block announcements or getdata responses to link the connections to the same physical node. This change partitions the compact block cache by network key (CNode::m_network_key), generating distinct nonces lazily for each network interface. The vulnerability was initially reported by ajtowns on IRC, and the PR includes functional tests demonstrating nonce separation across distinct binds.
evidence: Author notes the fingerprinting vector was reported by ajtowns on IRC.
Functional test in diff (`test_compactblock_nonce_per_network`) reproduces the issue by demonstrating that connections across different bind ports previously received identical nonces.
problem: Nodes currently reuse a single compact block nonce across all peers when serving the latest tip block from cache. An adversary connecting across different network types (such as IPv4 and Tor) can request the tip via `getdata(MSG_CMPCT_BLOCK)` or observe high-bandwidth announcements and compare nonces to link the connections and deanonymize the node.

risk.why: A flaw in compact block caching or serialization during block announcement could stall block relay to peers or cause peers to disconnect.

summary: Generate separate compact block nonces per network interface or bind address rather than sharing a single nonce across all peers. Cached compact block representations (`CBlockHeaderAndShortTxIDs`) are now constructed and serialized lazily per network key.
